Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:61: They said, at the hour a person departs from the world, it is not enough that he is terrified by the Angel of Death, who is full of eyes all over with his sword drawn in his hand, but he asks him: did you occupy yourself with Torah and acts of loving-kindness, and did you crown your Master [in Shema] morning and evening, and did you crown your fellow with a pleasant spirit? If these things are in him, he casts that drop into his mouth and his soul departs without pain, like drawing a hair out of milk; and if these things are not in him, his soul goes out from his body like the tearing of thorns from wool. And when the Angel of Death comes, he says to him: righteous one, your Master has sent me to you. Immediately he pleads with him. He says to him: this hour cannot be passed over, but I have heard from behind the curtain that the Holy One, blessed be He, is preparing a dwelling for you in the Garden of Eden.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:63: At the hour of judgment, the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the person: it was a great labor for Me over you, from when I formed you in your mother's womb and you were not stillborn; and when you emerged into the air of the world, I prepared sustenance for you and saved you from suffering - did you occupy yourself with Torah and perform acts of loving-kindness before Me? If these things are in him, they release him immediately from judgment; and if not, they hand him over to five angels of destruction, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. One strikes and one counts, the way they strike and count in a court; and a third brings forth fire from his body like a furnace from which fire emerges; the fourth brings bitter and sour herbs from the mountains, so that if he stole from his fellow, he says to him: grind carefully with your teeth, for you ate stolen food with your teeth. The fifth strikes his father and mother, and says to them: why did you not guide your children to study Torah and good deeds, so that he would perform commandments and good deeds and refrain from evil deeds? Immediately they give him permission to strike his father and mother; and if [the son] recited [Torah] but did not fulfill it, they flog him before them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:64: And although the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, need no strengthening, and are self-authenticating, for their words are spoken with the holy spirit and are the words of the living God, nevertheless I have seen fit to write these lines to arouse those who sleep.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:65: I, the writer, in the year 5330 [1570], in the month of Elul, in a dream at night there came to me a soul from that other world, about three months after its departure, and I recognized that he was dead, and I would ask him about the matters of that world, and he would tell me at length about the matters of the beating of the grave; and afterward he would tell me that in that world they judge and punish for the precision of details far more than a person would imagine in his mind - and let those who remain hear and fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:66: And concerning the judgment of the grave, Rashbi explains (Terumah 151a) that as long as the body remains in the grave, the soul is judged in Gehinnom, and after the body decomposes, the soul has rest. And they said: and therefore, how good it is for them, both for the righteous and for the wicked, that their body cling to the earth and decompose into dust within a short time, and not endure for a long period - in order that body and spirit not be judged continuously every single day; for there is no righteous person in the world who does not have the judgment of the grave, since that angel appointed over graves stands over the body and judges it every single day - if so for the righteous, how much more so for the wicked. Therefore, all the while the body decomposes and decays into dust, the judgment settles from everything - except for those pious ones who stand in the world who are fit to ascend to their Master with their souls, to that supernal place suited for them, and they are few in the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:67: And in Parashat Shelach Lecha (169b) he explains that of this it is said (Zechariah 3:3), "and Joshua was clothed in filthy garments" - this is the body of flesh, which is from the side of Samael, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 4:5; see Zohar there 172b), "the fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh." And while the body, which is from the side of Samael, still exists, they do not clothe the soul in the garment fitting for it in the Garden of Eden; and after the flesh is decomposed, then they clothe it in its garment - and this is (Zechariah 3:4-5), "remove the filthy garments from him," and so on, "and they clothed him with garments, and the angel of the LORD stood by" - for it is from the Shechinah, called "the angel of the LORD," that the garment is given to the soul. Therefore a person must diminish the flesh, which is from the husk, and increase in the repair of the garment of his soul, which endures forever, in the world that is entirely long.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:1: <small>In explaining the particulars of the punishments for which they are punished in Gehinnom, as found written in the Zohar and the Midrashim, and what the matter of Gehinnom is.</small>
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:2: The fire of Gehinnom, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 13b), is drawn from the River of Fire; in these words: "behold, the storm-wind of the LORD, wrath, has gone forth" - this is the River of Fire. From where does it emerge? Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said: from the sweat of the Chayot [the celestial beasts]. And to where is it poured out? Rav Chilkiyah bar Tovi said: upon the heads of the wicked in Gehinnom, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:19), "behold, the storm-wind of the LORD, wrath, has gone forth, a sweeping storm, it shall whirl upon the head of the wicked" - to the extent of these words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:3: Further, Isaiah the prophet revealed to us the matter of Gehinnom when he said (Isaiah 30:33), "for Tophet has long been ordained; it too has been prepared for the king; he has made it deep and large, its firepit has much fire and wood," and so on. And further, close to this prophecy, he says just before it (ibid. 31:9), "says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem." And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Midrash Aggadat Shmuel (Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 41), on the verse "for Tophet has long been ordained," and so on, "he has made it deep and large" - Rabbi Pinchas and Rabbi Chunya said: because the wicked say, how many tens of thousands does Gehinnom hold - two hundred myriads, three hundred myriads? How many wicked are there in every single generation? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: to the extent that you multiply in the world, so it too is enlarged every day and widens and deepens, as it is said, "for Tophet has long been ordained," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:4: And in the Zohar (Terumah 150b) this matter is explained, and it says that the fire of Gehinnom burns only because the wicked heat themselves with the fire of their inclination; in these words: Rabbi Yehuda said, the judgment of the punishments of Gehinnom - we have learned that it judges the wicked there - for what are they judged in the fire of Gehinnom? Rather, Gehinnom is a fire that burns day and night, corresponding to how the wicked heat themselves with the fire of the evil inclination to transgress the words of the Torah; with every single heating that they heat themselves with the evil inclination, so it burns with the fire of Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:5: Once, the evil inclination was not found in the world, for they had shut it within an iron seal in the aperture of the great abyss, and all that time the fire of Gehinnom was extinguished and did not burn at all. Once the evil inclination returned to its place, the wicked of the world began to heat themselves with it, the fire of Gehinnom began to burn - for Gehinnom burns only with the heat of the strength of the wicked's evil inclination, and with that heat Gehinnom burns day and night without settling.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:6: Seven gates has Gehinnom, and seven compartments are there; seven kinds of wicked people are there: the evil one, the worthless one, the sinner, the wicked one, the destroyer, the scoffer, the arrogant one - and corresponding to them all there are compartments in Gehinnom, each and every one as fits it, and according to the level at which that wicked person sinned, so they give him a compartment in Gehinnom. And in every single compartment there is an angel appointed over that place, under the authority of Dumah, and with him thousands and myriads who judge the wicked, each one as befits him in that compartment where he is.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:7: The fire of the lower Gehinnom reaches down from within the fire of the upper Gehinnom, and reaches that lower Gehinnom, and it is kindled by that arousal of the heat of the wicked, who heat themselves through the evil inclination, and all those compartments burn there - to this point. And it says that the fire of the lower Gehinnom reaches down from within the fire of the upper Gehinnom: the secret is that the upper Gehinnom is the River of Fire in which souls are refined, as is explained in Parashat Vayakhel, which we will copy further; and that River of Fire descends to the Gehinnom in the earth, which, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained, has three gates; and the wicked, through their heating, cause the fire of the upper River of Fire to be drawn down below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:8: And concerning the three gates that Gehinnom has, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in [tractate] Eruvin (19a), in these words: Rabbi Yirmiyah said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: Gehinnom has three gates - one in the wilderness, one in the sea, and one in Jerusalem. In the wilderness, as it is written (Numbers 16:33), "and they went down, they and all that belonged to them, alive, into Sheol." In the sea, as it is written (Jonah 2:3), "out of the belly of Sheol I cried out." In Jerusalem, as it is written (Isaiah 31:9), "whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem" - and it was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: "whose fire is in Zion" - this is the gate of Gehinnom. And is there no more? But is there not also what Rabbi Maryon said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and some say it was taught by Rav Mari, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai: there are two palm trees in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, and smoke rises between them, and this is what we learned, "the thorns of the Iron Mountain are fit [for a lulav]," and this is the gate of Gehinnom? Perhaps this is the one in the wilderness [i.e., the same gate].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:9: And the wicked person who would deny the matter of Gehinnom, let us tell him to go to the wilderness, to the fissures of Korach, as they said in Bava Batra (74a) in the tales of Rabbah bar bar Chanah: he said to me, come, I will show you those swallowed by Korach. I saw two cracks [fissures], and smoke was coming out of them. I took a tuft of wool and soaked it in water and stuck it on the head of a spear and put it in there, and when I took it out it was scorched. He said to me: listen, what do you hear? And I heard them saying: Moses is true and his Torah is true, and they [we] are liars. He said to me: every thirty days Gehinnom brings them back here like meat in a pot, and they say thus: Moses is true and his Torah is true, and they [we] are liars - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:10: Further, the matter of Gehinnom has been further verified through several tales that occurred in our own generation, and our forebears too told us of it, and we will not elaborate, so as not to depart from our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:11: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said (there in Eruvin): Gehinnom has seven names, and these are they: Sheol, Avaddon, Be'er Shachat [Well of the Pit], Bor Sha'on [Pit of Tumult], Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay], Tzalmavet [Shadow of Death], and Eretz Tachtit [Nethermost Land]. Sheol, as it is written (Jonah 2:3), "out of the belly of Sheol I cried out." Avaddon, as it is written (Psalms 88:12), "shall Your loving-kindness be told in the grave, Your faithfulness in Avaddon?" Be'er Shachat, as it is written (ibid. 55:24), "but You, O God, shall bring them down to the well of the pit." Bor Sha'on and Tit HaYaven, as it is written (ibid. 40:3), "and He brought me up out of the pit of tumult, out of the miry clay," and so on. Tzalmavet, as it is written (ibid. 107:10), "those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death." Eretz Tachtit - from the Gemara [without a specific verse cited].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:12: And is there also "Gehinnom" [itself as a name]? A valley [gei] that is as deep as the Valley of [Ben] Hinnom; another interpretation, that whoever descends into it descends on account of matters of "chinam" [gratuitous sin/for nothing]. And is there also "Tophet"? As it is said (Isaiah 30:33), "for Tophet has long been ordained" - because whoever is enticed [mitpateh] by his inclination falls there - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:13: Further, they said in the Midrash (Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 41): "for behold, those who are far from You shall perish" (Psalms 73:27) - David said, since one who is far from You in this world is lost in the World to Come. "You have cut off all who go astray [zonah] from You" - the wicked who declare themselves finally cut off [machlitin] through their sins and estrange themselves from You - so too, what do You do to them? You declare them finally cut off [machlitan] for Gehinnom; and "hitzmatah" [cut off] is a term meaning "final, absolute," as it is said (Leviticus 25:30), "in perpetuity [litzmitut] to the one who bought it" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:14: And since we have spoken of the matter of Gehinnom, I have seen fit to copy here Tractate Gehinnom, which I found among the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in a manuscript.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:16: It is written (Nahum 1:6), "before His indignation, who can stand? And who can endure the fierceness of His anger?" Rabbi Zeira opened: "the leech has two daughters, 'give, give'" (Proverbs 30:15). Rabbi Elazar said: two companies of angels stand at the gates of Gehinnom and say, give, give; bring, bring. And why is it called Gehinnom [Gei-Hinnom]? Because the sound of its roar [nehamatah] goes from one end of the world to the other. And why is it called Tophet? Because everyone enters there through the enticement [pituy] of the evil inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:18: Rabbi Yochanan opened (Psalms 84:7), "passing through the valley of weeping, they make it a place of springs; the early rain also covers it with blessings" - this teaches that the wicked confesses just as the leper confesses, and says: I, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, committed such-and-such a transgression, in such-and-such a place, on such-and-such a day, before so-and-so, in the presence of so-and-so and so-and-so.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:19: Three gates has Gehinnom: one in the sea, one in the wilderness, and one in the settled land. From where do we know the one in the sea? As it is said (Jonah 2:3), "out of the belly of Sheol I cried out; You heard my voice." From where do we know the one in the wilderness? As it is said (Numbers 16:33), "and they went down, they and all that belonged to them, alive, into Sheol." From where do we know the one in the settled land? As it is said (Isaiah 31:9), "says the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:20: There are five kinds of fire in Gehinnom: fire that consumes and drinks; that drinks and does not consume; that consumes and does not drink; that neither consumes nor drinks; and there is fire that consumes fire. There are coals in it as large as mountains, and coals in it as large as hills, and coals in it as large as the Dead Sea, and coals in it as large as great stones; there are rivers of pitch and sulfur in it, flowing and boiling in successive surges.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:21: [When] the sentence of a wicked man [is decreed], angels of destruction thrust him forward on his face, and others receive him from them and thrust him before the fire of Gehinnom, and it opens its mouth and swallows him, as it is said (Isaiah 5:14), "therefore Sheol has enlarged its desire and opened its mouth without limit, and her glory and her multitude and her tumult, and he who rejoices in her, shall go down into it" - this is for one who has no single merit to tip the scale in his favor. But one who has Torah and good deeds, and many sufferings come upon him, is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it is said (Psalms 23:4), "even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" - "Your rod," these are the sufferings; "Your staff," this is the Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:23: Rabbi Yochanan opened (Job 11:20), "but the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and escape shall be lost to them, and their hope shall be the expiring of the soul" - a body that is not consumed, and its soul goes out in a fire that is not quenched; and of them Scripture says (Isaiah 66:24), "for their worm shall not die, nor their fire be quenched."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:24: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: once I was walking on the road, and Elijah the prophet, remembered for good, found me. He said to me: do you wish that I stand you at the gate of Gehinnom? I said to him, yes. He showed me people hanging by their noses, and people hanging by their hands, and people hanging by their tongues, and people hanging by their feet; and he showed me women hanging by their breasts; and he showed me people hanging by their eyes; and he showed me people whom they were feeding their own flesh, and people whom they were feeding burning coals of broom-wood, and people sitting alive while worms ate them. He said to me: these are the ones of whom it is written, "for their worm shall not die." And he showed me people whom they were feeding fine sand, and they were forcing them to eat it and their teeth were breaking, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saying to them: wicked ones, when you ate stolen food it was sweet in your mouths, and now you have no strength to eat - to fulfill what is said (Psalms 3:8), "You have broken the teeth of the wicked."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:25: And he showed me people whom they were casting from the fire to the snow and from the snow to the fire, like a shepherd who drives his flock from mountain to mountain; and of them Scripture says (Psalms 49:15), "like sheep they are appointed for Sheol, death shall shepherd them, and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning, and their form shall be for Sheol to consume, that it have no habitation."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:26: Rabbi Yochanan said: every single angel is appointed to exact the punishment for one transgression; this one comes and judges him and departs, and so the second, and so the third, and so all of them, until they complete [judging] all the transgressions in his hand. A parable: to what may this be compared? To a debtor who had many creditors, and they brought him before the king. The king said to them: what shall I do for you? Go and divide him among yourselves. At that moment his soul is handed over in Gehinnom to cruel angels, who divide it among themselves.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:28: It is taught: three descend to Gehinnom and do not ascend - one who consorts with a married woman, one who whitens [shames] his fellow's face in public, and one who swears falsely by the name of the LORD; and some say, also one who honors himself through his fellow's disgrace, and one who stirs up discord between a man and his wife to bring strife between them. Every Sabbath eve they are led to two mountains of snow and left there, and at the conclusion of the Sabbath they are returned to their place, and an angel comes forth and thrusts them and returns them to their place in Gehinnom. And from it [the snow] they take some and place it beneath their armpits, to cool themselves during the six weekdays, and the Holy One, blessed be He, says to them: wicked ones, woe to you, that even in Gehinnom you steal! As it is said (Job 24:19), "drought and heat consume the snow waters; so does Sheol those who have sinned" - meaning, even in Sheol they sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:30: After twelve months they are turned to ash, and the wind scatters them beneath the feet of the righteous, as it is written (Malachi 3:21), "and you shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet." And afterward their souls return to them, and they go out from Gehinnom with their faces black as the bottom of a pot, and they justify the judgment upon themselves and say: rightly have You decreed against us, rightly have You judged us; to You, O LORD, belongs righteousness, and to us shame of face, as at this day.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:31: But the nations of the world, the idol-worshippers, are judged in seven compartments of fire, and in every single compartment, twelve months; and the River of Fire goes forth from beneath the Throne of Glory and descends upon them, going from one end of the world to the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:32: And seven compartments are in Gehinnom, and in every single compartment there are six thousand houses, and in every single house there are six thousand windows, and in every single window there are six thousand jars of gall, and all of them are prepared for the scribes and the judges; and of that hour Solomon said, "and I shall be innocent in the end" - and not one of them escapes unless he has Torah and good deeds.
